pr_body:
This provides an implementation of a HTTP Handler Adaptor that is coded directly to the Eclipse Jetty core API, bypassing any servlet implementation.

Fixes #32035
pr_title: Implement Eclipse Jetty core HTTP handler adapter

review_comment:
This `Lock` got my attention because pessimistic locking is usually not the first go-to method in Reactive Streams. Instead it's usually some sort of optimistic locking with a CAS loop.

That said, the lock protects 2 critical sections that represent quick state checks and updates. There is precedent for that sort of things, e.g. in `Reactor`, so in that case I think it is fine (although care will need to be exercised if the code is modified or new usage of the lock is introduced).

I'm wondering about the choice to extend `AbstractWebSocketSession` rather than `AbstractListenerWebSocketSession` which implements the receiving logic. This relates to @simonbasle's question as well with the resulting implementation using a `Lock`.

@lachlan-roberts 
can you look at the websocket part of these review

The JettyWebSocket API uses a demand model instead of suspend/resume.

The `AbstractListenerWebSocketSession` requires us to implement `suspendReceiving()` and `resumeReceiving()` so we're better off not extending that class.
Ah yes! Suspend/resume is intrinsically racy and best avoided.

If the headers is copied into LinkedMultiValueMap directly, it will break the case insensitive behavior of header names.

e.g.: If the headers contain an entry `content-type: application/json`(HTTP2 requires header names with lowercase), and the result of `headers.getContentType()` or `headers.getFirst("Content-Type")` will be null forever.
Can you raise this as a new issue?
indeed, thanks for the feedback! I've created issue #33666 to track and fix this in RC2
